issues.problem: 0.8 is not supported by the record's own gaps: no re-measured DRC count, no PR link, no confirmation the change was merged, and the issue closed as not_planned/Stale (typically 'abandoned', not 'resolved'). The field is also ambiguous about what it's rating -- fidelity of the quoted exchange vs. validity of the outcome.
issues.fix: Lower confidence to roughly 0.35-0.45 and explicitly scope it (e.g. 'confidence that the described exchange occurred as summarized; NOT a claim that the fix was validated').

issues.problem: Two independent parameter changes (layer adjustment 0.45->0.2 AND congestion iterations 30->35) are reported as a single fix, but the hypothesis field lists them as separate suspected causes. No ablation isolates which change (or their interaction) produced the outcome.
issues.fix: Reword to state explicitly that the two changes were applied together and the causal contribution of each is unconfirmed/confounded.

issues.problem: The quoted text uses an ellipsis joining what read as two distinct remarks ('...finish GRT by changing...0.45 to 0.2... We also changed...iterations to 35...') under a single date and a single non-comment-specific locator. This presents a possibly non-contiguous composite as a verbatim quote.
issues.fix: Split into two direct_quote objects, each with its own comment-permalink locator and date, or explicitly label the merged text as a paraphrased composite rather than a verbatim quote.

issues.problem: All three fields point to the bare issue URL with no comment anchor (e.g. #issuecomment-XXXXXXX), despite the entire causal claim resting on one specific comment.
issues.fix: Replace with a comment-level permalink for the quoted remark; reserve the bare issue URL for the issue-level context fields only.

issues.problem: The sentence 'We (eder-matheus) note the layer-adjustment is documented at set-global-routing-layer-adjustment...' fuses the annotator's first-person voice with the source engineer's username, producing an ungrammatical and unattributable claim.
issues.fix: Rewrite as either 'eder-matheus notes that the layer-adjustment mechanism is documented at set-global-routing-layer-adjustment' (attributed to the source) or as a plain annotator aside with no username inserted -- pick one voice.

issues.problem: The record asserts 0.45 is 'too aggressive' and that lowering to 0.2 fixed it, but never states the parameter's polarity (whether a higher or lower adjustment value reduces routing capacity more). The causal story is asserted, not shown to be internally consistent.
issues.fix: State explicitly, using only what the thread provides, which direction of the adjustment value corresponds to more capacity reduction, so the 'too aggressive -> lowered -> fixed' narrative is verifiably coherent rather than assumed.

issues.problem: The title frames '20k DRCs at only 0.24 density' as an inherent paradox, but the observation itself explains the congestion as localized (top of die, around the macro) rather than density-driven globally -- localized congestion at low global density is not actually surprising, so the framing oversells the anomaly the record's own body resolves.
issues.fix: Reframe title/observation to 'localized routing congestion despite low global placement density' rather than implying the raw density number itself is the anomaly.

issues.problem: The magnitude figures ('20k DRCs', '0.24 density') are stated as flat fact with no indication of which part of the thread (title line, a specific comment, a log excerpt) they were pulled from, unlike the fix claim which has an attributed quote.
issues.fix: Add a locator or note indicating the source line for these numbers, or mark them as thread-title-derived if that's their origin.

recommendation: Revise before inclusion: recalibrate confidence, deconfound the intervention, fix quote segmentation/locators, repair the garbled attribution in gaps, and soften the density-paradox framing in the title.
